name: Evident Insights landing page for its AI benchmarking platform and Evident AI Index
title: Evident Insights landing page for its AI benchmarking platform and Evident AI Index
answer: Evident Insights publishes this landing page for its intelligence platform, which benchmarks and tracks AI adoption across financial services. Its most useful point for banking readers is that the Evident AI Index for Banks, launched in January 2023, is returning with 2026 results in October, and regional versions cover Latin America and the Middle East and Africa. The page also promotes insurance results, reports, an invitation only symposium and a newsletter with over 15,000 subscribers, but it does not publish rankings, scores or methodology here.

sections.body: Evident Insights Ltd publishes this page. It is a landing page for Evident Insights, which the text describes as an intelligence platform that benchmarks and tracks AI adoption across financial services. Its scope is financial services, with named coverage of banks and insurance and regional banking indexes for Latin America and the Middle East and Africa. The page carries a 2026 copyright, refers to 2026 indexes and events, and says the Evident AI Index launched in January 2023. The text was harvested on 26 September 2026.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page says Evident benchmarks deployment across the sector, spotlights emerging trends and equips leaders with insights to accelerate AI transformation. It offers data, research and benchmarking. It promotes the Evident AI Index for Banks, which returns in October 2026, and asks readers to register interest to know when results go live. It also lists a 2026 Evident AI Index for Insurance, a Latin America banks report, an inaugural MEA banks index, and an invitation only Evident AI Symposium 2026 for senior AI leaders in finance. The Evident Banking Brief newsletter covers trends in AI and financial services and has over 15,000 subscribers across banking, tech, consulting, academia and government. The page states that since launching in January 2023, the Evident AI Index has generated debate and wide spread press coverage, with CEO Alexandra Mousavizadeh a regular commentator on global AI trends. It also carries short editorial statements: tech companies have hogged the spotlight in the initial wave of AI hype, several of the world's biggest banks have quietly become AI powered behemoths, AI is breathing new life into Wall Street's tech hiring scene, landing a software job in finance is more challenging than in recent years, and banks are racing to incorporate AI into almost everything they do.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives these specifics: the Evident AI Index launched in January 2023; the 2026 Evident AI Index for Banks returns in October; there are 2026 insurance results and an inaugural MEA banks index; the Evident Banking Brief has over 15,000 subscribers; and CEO Alexandra Mousavizadeh is named as a regular commentator on global AI trends. It also states positions that banks have quietly become AI powered behemoths and that banks are racing to incorporate AI into almost everything they do. It gives no bank rankings, scores, metric definitions or methodology.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in banking would use this page to locate Evident's banking benchmark and related reports. It signals that the Evident AI Index for Banks is a recurring publication, with 2026 results due in October, and that Evident also covers Latin America and the Middle East and Africa. It points to insurance and financial services coverage, an invitation only symposium and a newsletter as ways to follow the sector. The page supports the idea that banks are adopting AI broadly and competing for technology talent, but it is a signpost to future results rather than a source of current bank standings.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Banking

sections.body: This is a commercial landing page for Evident Insights products, events and newsletter, not a research report. It does not provide the index methodology, bank level scores, rankings, metric definitions or findings. Its statements about banks becoming AI powered behemoths and about tech hiring are brief editorial claims without supporting data on the page. It covers financial services broadly, including insurance, so banking specific detail is limited. Some 2026 results are described as forthcoming, and the page is dated by its 2026 copyright and September 2026 harvest.
